divergence_classification.name: Adequate thesis
divergence_classification.triage_target: evidence and support — identifying what the claim requires the reader to believe and what information would supply that reason

classification.note: Both moves legitimately advance the student from thesis to support-building, differing only in entry angle — exhaustive targets subclaim formation while triage targets evidence identification — neither is clearly higher-leverage at this developmental stage.

divergence_classification.name: Strong thesis that should not be over-taught
divergence_classification.exhaustive_target: Release to continue drafting; light forward orientation toward body paragraph purpose.
divergence_classification.triage_target: development — moving from a sharp opening claim to supporting reasoning and evidence

classification.note: Both responses affirm the draft's strength and forward-orient toward body paragraph development; triage asks the student to draft next sentences while exhaustive withholds that nudge, a difference in degree of scaffolding rather than a meaningful quality gap.

divergence_classification.name: Evidence without explanation
divergence_classification.exhaustive_target: Explanation / Analysis — interpreting evidence to connect it to the claim

classification.note: Both moves correctly diagnose the same foundational gap (evidence lacks interpretive connection to claim) and invite the student to supply their own reasoning; phrasing and entry point differ but leverage and safety are equivalent.

divergence_classification.name: Weak transition
divergence_classification.exhaustive_target: Naming the relationship between two adjacent sentences (transition as conceptual relationship).
divergence_classification.triage_target: logical connection between ideas (inside-out clarification of intended reasoning sequence before transitions can be addressed)

classification.note: Exhaustive jumps to labeling inter-sentence relationships (outside-in surface fix) before the student has demonstrated awareness of the underlying argument sequence; triage correctly asks the student to first articulate the logical chain, making any subsequent transition work meaningful rather than cosmetic.

divergence_classification.name: Sentence-level confusion
divergence_classification.exhaustive_target: Identify the sentence's central actor and main action as the foundation for revision
divergence_classification.triage_target: intended meaning / core idea — identifying the one thing the writer most wants to say about skateboarding

classification.note: Both moves correctly identify the same foundational problem (tangled ideas, no clear core message) and invite the writer to name the one central idea before revising; exhaustive frames it through the lens of actor/action structure while triage frames it as meaning-finding, but neither is clearly superior in leverage or safety.

divergence_classification.name: Student asks the AI to write the answer
divergence_classification.exhaustive_target: eliciting a position/stance as prerequisite to forming a thesis
divergence_classification.triage_target: Intended position / central claim — surfacing what the student actually believes about free public transit

classification.note: Both moves correctly identify the same foundational prerequisite — surfacing the student's position before drafting — and differ only in minor phrasing and framing, with no meaningful difference in leverage or safety.

divergence_classification.name: Ambiguous: both-sides could be a legitimate nuanced thesis
divergence_classification.exhaustive_target: what counts as evidence/support for this claim (linking thesis to body)

classification.note: Both moves address the claim's argumentative strength at the same developmental level but use different entry points (falsifiability test vs. evidence-linking), making neither clearly superior for this already-strong draft.

divergence_classification.name: Ambiguous: reflective piece not needing a thesis
divergence_classification.exhaustive_target: Purpose articulation — helping the student name where the reflection is headed before developing further
divergence_classification.triage_target: grounding the reflective insight in concrete scene/supporting detail

classification.note: Both moves are defensible next steps for this early-stage draft — exhaustive surfaces destination/purpose before expansion, triage grounds the insight in concrete scene — neither is clearly higher-leverage given how undeveloped the draft is.

divergence_classification.name: Descriptive — flat detail, no dominant impression
divergence_classification.exhaustive_target: Sensory/concrete supporting detail — moving from inventory to experienced description
divergence_classification.triage_target: Unifying Impression / Dominant Mood (communicative purpose for descriptive writing)

classification.note: Triage correctly identifies the upstream problem — the student has no controlling impression yet — so coaching mood/purpose first prevents detail work from going in the wrong direction; exhaustive jumps to craft execution before the writer knows what they're trying to convey.

Both moves correctly identify the missing thesis/central claim as the foundational problem and invite the student to generate it themselves; the difference is framing (comparative dimension vs. authorial stance) rather than quality.

divergence_classification.name: Concession is a straw man
divergence_classification.exhaustive_target: Fair representation of the counterargument (no straw man)
divergence_classification.triage_target: representing opposing views fairly (steelmanning before rebutting)

classification.note: Both moves correctly identify the straw-man as the foundational problem and invite the student to steelman the opposition; triage is marginally more explicit about concrete counter-reasons but neither outperforms the other on leverage or safety.

divergence_classification.name: Conclusion introduces a new argument
divergence_classification.exhaustive_target: Eliminating the new-argument error and replacing it with synthesis/completion of the essay's actual purpose
divergence_classification.triage_target: conclusion function — synthesis vs. new-claim introduction

classification.note: Both moves correctly identify the new-argument error, explain the synthesis-vs-new-claim distinction, and redirect the student toward completing the essay's established purpose without coauthoring; differences are stylistic rather than substantive.

divergence_classification.name: Student pastes AI-generated text and asks 'is this good?'
divergence_classification.exhaustive_target: Thesis: move from topic-summary to contestable claim
divergence_classification.triage_target: authentic voice and intended meaning — what the student genuinely wants to argue

classification.note: Triage correctly identifies that the student's problem is borrowed academic language masking an absent genuine position, and routes to authentic voice before thesis-craft work can be meaningful; exhaustive jumps to thesis mechanics on a sentence that may not yet represent what the student actually thinks.

divergence_classification.name: Perfectionist stuck — won't commit anything
divergence_classification.exhaustive_target: Elicit a rough stance/position sentence to break the block

classification.note: Both moves competently address the block with a low-stakes generative prompt; triage uses open-ended freewrite while exhaustive offers a sentence-stem scaffold, but neither is clearly superior for this stage.
